breakfast.name: Ful Medames
ingredients: 2 cups dried fava beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked fava beans and place in a pot with fresh water.
Boil until very tender, about 25-30 minutes, then drain most of the water.
Mash some of the beans lightly, leaving some whole for texture.
Heat peanut oil and sauté onion until golden. Add garlic and cumin.
Fold the onion mixture into the beans along with diced tomatoes.
Season with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Serve in bowls drizzled with extra oil and garnished with parsley alongside warm flatbread.
breakfast.description: Slow-cooked fava beans mashed and seasoned with cumin, lemon, and peanut oil. A hearty Sudanese breakfast that fuels the morning.

breakfast.name: Gurasa with Egg
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Let stand for 10 minutes.
Mix flour and salt, add the yeast mixture and knead into a soft dough.
Let the dough rest for 30 minutes until doubled.
Divide into balls and roll each into a thin round.
Cook on a hot dry griddle until golden on both sides.
Scramble eggs with butter, onion, and tomato.
Serve the gurasa topped with the scrambled egg mixture.
breakfast.description: Soft, spongy Sudanese flatbread served with scrambled eggs, onion, and tomato. A simple yet satisfying morning meal.

breakfast.name: Ful Medames with Lime
ingredients: Dried fava beans (soaked overnight and cooked)
Lime juice, olive oil or sesame oil
instructions: Ful medames is the Egyptian and Sudanese staple bean breakfast
One of the oldest continuously prepared dishes in the world
Sudan and Egypt share this dish -- the Nile connection
The fava beans are cooked until very soft
Dressed with lime, oil, garlic, and cumin
Eaten with kisra flatbread or bread
breakfast.description: Sudanese fava bean breakfast -- ful medames (one of the world oldest continuously prepared dishes), fava beans cooked until soft and dressed with lime, sesame oil, garlic, and cumin. Sudan and Egypt share this dish via the Nile. Eaten with kisra or bread.

breakfast.name: Bajiya (Falafel-Type Fritters)
ingredients: Dried fava beans or chickpeas (soaked, ground)
instructions: Bajiya are Sudanese falafel-type fritters
Ground fava beans or chickpeas with herbs and spices
Fried in hot oil
Sold by street vendors in the morning
Eaten in bread as a sandwich
breakfast.description: Sudanese ground fava bean fritters -- similar to Egyptian falafel, ground soaked beans with parsley, coriander, cumin, and chilli, fried in hot oil. Sold by street vendors in the morning and eaten in bread as a sandwich.

lunch.name: Mulah Bamia (Okra Stew)
instructions: Heat peanut oil and brown the lamb cubes on all sides.
Add onions and garlic, cook until softened.
Stir in tomato puree, tomato paste, coriander, and cardamom.
Add enough water to cover the meat, drop in the dried lime.
Simmer for 30 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the okra and cook for another 15-20 minutes until everything is tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve over steamed white rice.
lunch.description: A rich Sudanese lamb and okra stew cooked with dried lime and warm spices. The okra adds body to the sauce while the lamb provides deep flavor.

lunch.name: Kisra with Mullah
instructions: Mix sorghum flour with water to form a thin, smooth batter. Let it ferment for a few hours.
Heat a flat pan and pour a thin layer of batter, spreading it in a circular motion. Cook until set and peel off. Repeat.
For the mullah, heat oil and brown beef cubes.
Add onions and cook until caramelized. Add tomatoes and cook down.
Stir in peanut butter, cumin, and chili flakes. Add water as needed.
Simmer until beef is tender and sauce is thick, about 30 minutes.
Serve the mullah over folded kisra.
lunch.description: Thin, slightly tangy sorghum crepes paired with a hearty beef and peanut butter stew. Kisra is the staple bread of Sudan.

lunch.name: Mullah (Meat Stew)
instructions: Mullah is the Sudanese meat stew -- the everyday protein dish
Lamb or goat braised with onions and tomatoes
Cumin and coriander are the dominant spices
Served with asida (stiff porridge) or bread
lunch.description: Sudanese meat stew -- lamb or goat braised with onion, tomatoes, and cumin-coriander spices. The everyday Sudanese protein dish. Served with asida (stiff sorghum porridge) or bread.

lunch.name: Tamiya Sandwich (Sudanese Falafel)
instructions: Tamiya is the Sudanese version of falafel -- made from fava beans, not chickpeas
Eaten in a bread roll with tomato and tahini
The Sudanese street food sandwich
Sold at Sudanese breakfast stalls
lunch.description: Sudanese falafel sandwich -- ground fava bean fritters (tamiya) in a bread roll with tomato, cucumber, and tahini. The Sudanese street food breakfast. Fava beans, not chickpeas, distinguish it from Lebanese falafel.

lunch.name: Karkade (Hibiscus Soup)
instructions: Karkade is the Sudanese hibiscus drink -- drunk hot or cold
The deep ruby color from the hibiscus petals
Tart and floral -- refreshing in the Sudanese heat
Also used in Sudanese cooking as a souring agent
Drunk hot in winter; cold in summer
The national drink of Sudan and Egypt
lunch.description: Sudanese hibiscus drink -- karkade, dried hibiscus flowers steeped in water, sweetened and served hot (winter) or cold (summer). Deep ruby color, tart and floral. Used as a souring agent in cooking as well. The national drink of Sudan.

dinner.name: Shaiyah (Grilled Lamb)
ingredients: 1kg lamb leg, cut into large pieces
instructions: Mix grated onion, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, cardamom, oil, salt, and pepper into a marinade.
Coat the lamb pieces thoroughly and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Prepare a charcoal grill or preheat a grill to high heat.
Grill the lamb pieces, turning occasionally, until charred on the outside and cooked through, about 25-30 minutes.
Let the meat rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve with flatbread, fresh salad, and tahini sauce.
dinner.description: Charcoal-grilled lamb marinated in a blend of Sudanese spices. A celebratory dish often prepared for gatherings and special occasions.

dinner.name: Agashe (Meat and Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and brown the beef on all sides.
Add onions and cook until translucent.
Stir in tomato puree, tomato paste, cumin, and coriander.
Add enough water to cover the meat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add potatoes, carrots, and eggplant. Cook for 15 minutes.
Add zucchini and cook for another 10 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Serve hot with kisra or steamed rice.
dinner.description: A comforting Sudanese one-pot stew brimming with beef and seasonal vegetables in a rich tomato-spice broth.

dinner.name: Miris (Lamb Ribs)
instructions: Lamb ribs grilled over charcoal -- simple Sudanese grilled meat
The ribs are spiced simply and grilled over coal fire
Served with lemon and flatbread
Eaten at Sudanese restaurants and home grills
dinner.description: Sudanese grilled lamb ribs -- simply spiced with cumin, coriander, and black pepper, grilled over charcoal, served with lemon and flatbread. Straightforward grilled meat of the Sudanese restaurant.

dinner.name: Bamia (Okra Stew)
instructions: Bamia is the Sudanese okra stew
Fresh or dried okra with meat in a tomato-based stew
The okra mucilage thickens the stew
Bamia is eaten from Egypt to Sudan to Ethiopia
Served with flatbread or asida
dinner.description: Sudanese okra stew -- fresh or dried okra cooked with lamb in a tomato-cumin stew. The okra mucilage thickens. Bamia is eaten from Egypt to Sudan. Served with flatbread.

dinner.name: Shiyya (Grilled Meat Platter)
instructions: Shiyya is the Sudanese grilled meat platter
Various cuts grilled over charcoal
Simply spiced -- the quality of the meat is the focus
Served with raw onion, lemon, and flatbread
A Sudanese restaurant staple
dinner.description: Sudanese grilled meat platter -- various lamb and beef cuts grilled over charcoal, simply spiced with cumin and black pepper, served with raw onion, lemon, and flatbread. The Sudanese restaurant staple.

snacks.name: Tamiya (Sudanese Falafel)
ingredients: 2 cups dried fava beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked fava beans and pulse in a food processor with onion, garlic, parsley, and cilantro until a coarse paste forms.
Season with cumin, coriander, salt, pepper, and baking soda. Mix well.
Shape into small patties and coat with sesame seeds.
Heat oil for deep frying to 180°C.
Fry the patties until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with tahini sauce and pickled vegetables.
snacks.description: Crispy, herb-packed fava bean fritters coated in sesame seeds. Sudan's version of falafel is a popular street snack eaten at any time of day.

snacks.name: Sesame Seeds (Sim Sim)
instructions: Sudan is one of the world largest sesame seed producers
The seeds are eaten roasted as a snack
Also pressed for sesame oil
Used in Sudanese cooking and as tahini
snacks.description: Sudanese roasted sesame seeds -- Sudan is one of the world largest sesame producers. Roasted seeds eaten as a simple snack, also pressed for oil or made into tahini.

snacks.name: Dates and Coffee
instructions: Jabana is the Sudanese coffee ceremony -- similar to the Ethiopian coffee ceremony
Coffee with cardamom and ginger
Served in small cups with dates
The hospitality ritual: the jabana is offered to every guest
The Sudanese coffee ceremony: multiple cups, slow, communal
snacks.description: Sudanese spiced coffee ceremony -- jabana (coffee with cardamom and ginger) served in small cups with dates. Similar to the Ethiopian ceremony. The hospitality ritual: offered to every guest. Multiple cups, communal and slow.

snacks.name: Groundnut Candy
instructions: Groundnut candy made with honey or caramelized sugar
The peanuts and sesame coated in caramelized sugar
Set into bars
A Sudanese sweet snack
snacks.description: Sudanese peanut-sesame candy -- roasted groundnuts and sesame seeds coated in caramelized sugar or honey, set into bars. A Sudanese street sweet.

desserts.name: Basbousa
ingredients: For syrup: 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp rose water
instructions: Mix semolina, sugar, yogurt, melted butter, baking powder, and vanilla into a thick batter.
Pour into a greased baking pan and smooth the top.
Score into diamond shapes and place an almond in the center of each.
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden.
While baking, prepare the syrup by boiling sugar and water, then adding lemon juice and rose water.
Pour the hot syrup over the hot basbousa immediately after removing from the oven.
Let it absorb the syrup for 30 minutes before serving.
desserts.description: A syrup-soaked semolina cake scented with rose water, each piece topped with a blanched almond. A popular Sudanese sweet for celebrations.

desserts.name: Um Ali (Egyptian-Sudanese Bread Pudding)
instructions: Um Ali is the Egyptian bread pudding -- also eaten in Sudan
Shredded puff pastry or bread baked in sweetened milk and cream
Mixed with raisins, nuts, and coconut
Baked until the top is golden
Rich and sweet
desserts.description: Sudanese-Egyptian bread pudding -- shredded puff pastry baked in sweetened milk and cream with raisins, nuts, and coconut. Um Ali is Egyptian in origin, also eaten in Sudan. Rich and comforting.

desserts.name: Halva (Sesame Sweet)
instructions: Halva is the sesame sweet -- eaten across the Arab world
Made from tahini (sesame paste) and sugar
Sudan: its sesame production makes this particularly local
Dense, crumbly, sweet, with intense sesame flavor
desserts.description: Sudanese sesame halva -- tahini (sesame paste) mixed with sugar and set into a dense, crumbly sweet. Sudan is one of the largest sesame producers; halva is particularly resonant here.

drinks.name: Hulu Mur (Spiced Hibiscus Drink)
instructions: Bring water to a boil and add dried hibiscus flowers.
Reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes until the water turns deep red.
Strain out the flowers.
Add sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Strain again and chill thoroughly.
Serve over ice cubes.
drinks.description: A deep crimson Sudanese drink made from steeped hibiscus flowers spiced with cinnamon and ginger. Refreshingly tart and sweet.

drinks.name: Araqi (Date Arak)
instructions: Pour the date arak into a glass.
Add cold water and watch the spirit turn a milky white (the louche effect).
Add ice cubes to taste.
Garnish with a fresh mint sprig.
Sip slowly alongside meze or grilled meats.
drinks.description: Sudan's traditional anise-flavored spirit distilled from dates. When mixed with water it turns a characteristic milky white, best enjoyed with savory dishes.

drinks.name: Aradaib (Tamarind Drink)
instructions: Aradaib is the Sudanese tamarind drink
The tamarind pods are soaked in water
The pulp is extracted and sweetened
Sour, refreshing, and deeply Sudanese
Sold at markets and street stalls
drinks.description: Sudanese tamarind drink -- dried tamarind pods soaked and pulp extracted, sweetened and served cold. Called aradaib. Sour, refreshing, and sold at every market and street stall.
